tasks.short: Refer major faults to service providers and coordinate their resolution.

steps.what: Check the incident history, device record and service entitlement.
Decide whether specialist service is needed and select the escalation route.
Assemble fault details, attempted fixes and relevant diagnostic attachments.

loop.input: Selected incident notes and diagnostic excerpts, with secrets removed.
loop.output: Source-linked fault summary and attempted fixes in a fixed request template.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; specialist checks accuracy and disclosure.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing evidence returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Chronological free-text notes need summarising; entitlement fields remain deterministic.

steps.what: Review disclosure and submit the service request through the provider's channel.
Agree service arrangements, clarify findings and resolve responsibility disputes.
Record the service reference, agreed plan and next follow-up date.

tasks.design: Configure the {HELPDESK} to join incident, asset and entitlement records and generate a service-request template. A bounded model drafts the fault narrative; the specialist approves disclosure before submission through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. Structured service references and agreed dates feed the {HELPDESK}, with reminders in the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Entitlements, diagnostic notes and provider channels were disconnected. Disputed responsibility still required a person.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing service workflows cover routing and reminders. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of missing connectors; bounded summarisation handles incident prose.
tasks.still_hard: Provider interfaces vary, and warranty disputes need judgement. GDPR requires controlled disclosure; paid work still follows purchasing authority.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparent device fault is a wider incident, and negotiating a workable service plan.

ambition.what: A weekly recurring-fault review proposing replacement or supplier action.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer evidence hunts and more stalled-case resolution. The specialist can prioritise recurring-fault investigations within the support remit; purchasing rights do not change.

reach.task: Coordinate updates during a prolonged service interruption.
reach.learn: Expectation setting, clear next-update commitments and complaint recovery.

evidence.claim: Ticket summarisation is available today; this supports request preparation, not autonomous service commitments.
Structured entitlement checks, routing and follow-up reminders can use configured workflows.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
The service desk has linked asset records and reusable escalation rules.
Submission covers an existing entitlement; new expenditure follows a separate approval.
Build ranges assume one service desk and one provider connection, including access review and any applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which provider channels support submission and status exchange?
Where are current entitlements and service references stored?
Who may approve diagnostic disclosure and chargeable work?
Does employee consultation apply to the proposed logging changes?
research_questions: Which required request fields can be populated through existing configuration?
What information can be excluded from diagnostic attachments without weakening fault assessment?
new_work: Review generated fault summaries and attachments.
Resolve unmatched entitlements and failed provider submissions.
Maintain routing rules, connector credentials and request templates.
Enter agreed service dates when conversations produce no structured record.

tasks.short: Evaluate hardware or software and recommend improvements or upgrades.

steps.what: Clarify user problems, constraints and evaluation criteria with stakeholders.
Gather specifications, support history, lifecycle dates and cost information.

loop.input: Selected specifications, quotes and lifecycle documents.
loop.output: A comparison table with source passages, dates, units and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate field types and units; verify consequential claims against cited passages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per document; unresolved fields remain unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents use inconsistent prose and layouts; structured records use direct mappings.

steps.what: Run representative compatibility, performance and usability tests with selected users.
Compare options against criteria and assess operational trade-offs.
Write the evaluation, recommendation and proposed upgrade sequence.

loop.input: Approved comparison data and the specialist's chosen recommendation.
loop.output: A report explaining evidence, trade-offs, uncertainties and upgrade sequence.
loop.check: Recalculate costs in code; check every factual claim against supplied evidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims are removed or marked unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining mixed technical and user evidence needs prose; calculations and tables remain deterministic.

steps.what: Discuss trade-offs and obtain a decision on the recommendation.
Record the decision, rationale and follow-up evaluation date.

tasks.design: Use a reusable evaluation brief and cost model in the {DOCS} and {SPREADSHEET}, with evidence drawn from the {HELPDESK} and {PROCUREMENT}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare comparisons and reports; the specialist runs tests and chooses the recommendation. The IT manager's decision creates a record and follow-up in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence collection and report preparation were repetitive, while evaluation criteria and test conditions changed between requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable schemas and calculation templates reduce setup. Bounded extraction handles document variation, and AI-assisted coding can make small evidence connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Representative trials, accessibility needs and migration risks remain context dependent. Staff usage data requires GDPR safeguards and any consultation required by national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing realistic tests and recognising when a technically stronger option would make users' work harder.

ambition.what: A quarterly evidence-based refresh shortlist for ageing equipment.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into collecting specifications and formatting reports; more goes into trials and migration advice. The specialist can initiate shortlist reviews within an agreed remit; budget approval remains with the IT manager.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Assess how an upgrade changes administrative workflows.
reach.learn: Task observation, service continuity and the cost of retraining.

evidence.claim: Prompted document metadata extraction exists, but its outputs can be wrong and require validation.
Comparison templates, cost calculations and repeatable test scripts can reduce evaluation preparation.
Developer field trials document productivity gains; they do not establish a 10-to-100-fold build improvement here.

assumptions: Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates requiring a local pilot.
The OTHER slot in testing means device diagnostics and software test utilities.
Quotes, specifications and incident history can be accessed lawfully.
Build scope covers one evaluation template and limited connectors, not a laboratory or procurement replacement.
Consent and access estimates include any consultation required under national rules; elapsed time may be longer.
unknowns: Which evaluation criteria and cost assumptions are already approved?
Are representative test devices, environments and users available?
Who can authorise trials and shortlist reviews?
Will the evaluation collect individual employee usage data?
research_questions: Which comparison fields can be obtained as structured exports?
Which tests predict actual user outcomes rather than benchmark scores?
How reliably do source-linked extractions preserve exclusions and lifecycle conditions?
new_work: Verify extracted specifications, exclusions and lifecycle dates.
Maintain cost assumptions and comparison templates.
Review whether prior recommendations achieved their expected outcomes.

tasks.short: Create practical technology guidance and teach users how to work with hardware and software.

steps.what: Review recurring support topics and existing guidance to identify training needs.
Confirm learners' tasks, starting knowledge and accessibility needs.
Draft instructions, screenshots, practice exercises and session materials.

loop.input: Approved procedures, sanitised screenshots and a defined learner task.
loop.output: A lesson, quick guide and practice exercise using a fixed template.
loop.check: Check source coverage, version labels and personal-data removal; test instructions in the target interface.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per lesson; unsupported instructions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting technical prose to learner knowledge needs language judgement; layout uses templates.

steps.what: Test the instructions and approve accurate, accessible learning materials.
Publish materials, arrange sessions and invite the intended learners.
Demonstrate tasks, observe practice and help learners overcome difficulties.
Record participation and send follow-up exercises and a feedback request.

tasks.design: Configure topic counts from the {HELPDESK} and reusable lesson templates in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares guidance from approved procedures; a specialist tests and approves it before the {LMS} publishes it and the {CALENDAR} schedules sessions. Configured follow-ups record participation and collect feedback while practical coaching stays human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing each guide and coordinating sessions took time. Existing material often lacked a clear version, owner or review date.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and configured learning workflows already handle publication and follow-up. Bounded drafting reduces adaptation work without claiming to understand each learner.
tasks.still_hard: Screenshots and instructions age quickly, and accessibility requires real testing. GDPR applies to learning records; national rules may require consultation when tracking changes.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing confusion, building confidence and changing the explanation while someone practises.

ambition.what: Short accessible onboarding lessons for shift workers who miss daytime sessions.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week coaching and testing whether guidance works. They can prioritise lesson topics within an agreed curriculum remit; employee performance decisions remain outside this task.

reach.task: Teach a user a repeatable self-service procedure.
reach.learn: Plain-language explanations, teach-back and recognition of accessibility barriers.

evidence.claim: Reviewed knowledge-item drafting is available today; this supports guidance preparation but does not establish teaching effectiveness.
A large internal self-service deployment reports fewer support tickets; its scale and baseline limit transfer to this company size.
Learning publication, enrolment and follow-up can use configured workflows.

assumptions: Step shares, remaining time and delivery ranges are planning estimates.
Topic counts use existing categories and aggregate demand rather than employee rankings.
The OTHER slot means the hardware or software interface being taught.
The audience is internal, so publication and invitations are internal writes.
Build scope covers one lesson family and existing learning software.
Access work includes GDPR review and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Which guidance is authoritative and who approves changes?
Which languages, accessibility needs and shifts must be covered?
Can the learning system publish materials and record attendance through configuration?
What participation data may be retained, and for how long?
research_questions: Which recurring questions would benefit from training rather than a software fix?
Can learners complete the target task after using the guide?
Which interface changes should trigger a material review?
new_work: Test generated instructions and practice exercises.
Maintain source procedures, screenshots and review dates.
Handle unanswered learner questions and update approved guidance.
Maintain enrolment rules and retention settings.

tasks.short: Check ordered equipment, test readiness and prepare it for user delivery.

steps.what: Read the approved order and identify the required equipment and accessories.
Match received serial numbers and quantities against the order and asset records.
Inspect equipment, ports, packaging and accessories for visible damage or omissions.
Connect equipment and run standard startup, peripheral and hardware diagnostics.
Decide whether equipment is ready or requires correction before delivery.
Update the asset record and delivery request with readiness and intended recipient.
Prepare the equipment label and packing checklist.
Attach the label, pack accessories and stage equipment for delivery.

tasks.design: Join approved orders in the {PROCUREMENT} to asset and delivery records in the {HELPDESK}, using deterministic serial-number and quantity checks. Configure diagnostic utilities represented by {OTHER} to return structured results, then require a specialist's release decision. Generate labels and packing checklists from approved records while physical inspection and packing remain hands-on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order, asset and diagnostic records were separate, and physical checks could not be replaced by paperwork automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured order exports, barcode capture and diagnostic results support ordinary integration. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and template work; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Unpacking, connecting, inspecting and packing remain physical. Missing serial numbers, unusual peripherals and unreliable diagnostics create exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting physical defects and recognising a device that passes diagnostics but is unsuitable for the user.

ambition.what: A ready-equipment pool for urgent replacements.

tasks.altitude: The week has fewer record checks and more equipment preparation and exception handling. Within an agreed stock allocation, the specialist can prioritise ready replacements; purchasing authority does not change.

reach.task: Coordinate equipment collection and confirm the intended recipient.
reach.learn: Collection scheduling, recipient checks and clear custody records.

evidence.claim: Structured order matching, diagnostic checklists and label generation can use deterministic technology.
Physical inspection and equipment handling remain manual without additional specialised hardware.

assumptions: Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Goods receipt already captures serial numbers, or existing barcode capture can supply them.
The OTHER slot means device-management and hardware-diagnostic utilities.
Supported diagnostics expose structured results; plugging in equipment remains human work.
Asset records are held in the service desk rather than an assumed spreadsheet.
Access estimates include GDPR review of recipient records and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Are received serial numbers captured reliably?
Which device and peripheral tests can run unattended?
Where are asset assignment and readiness recorded today?
Who authorises release and replacement-stock allocation?
Can existing printers and scanners use the generated labels?
research_questions: Which diagnostic failures reliably predict equipment rejection?
Can current configuration cover order matching before a connector is built?
Which physical checks prevent the most delivery rework?
new_work: Resolve unmatched serial numbers and order discrepancies.
Maintain equipment standards and diagnostic checklists.
Check failed or incomplete diagnostic runs.
Maintain label templates and connector mappings.
Review release exceptions and replacement-pool stock accuracy.

role.altitude: The role shifts from assembling records and paperwork toward difficult faults, representative testing and practical coaching. Proposed delegation covers review priorities, lesson topics and replacement allocation within agreed limits; spending and broader policy decisions stay with their existing approvers.
reach: Customer service representatives: service recovery and clear technical explanations.
First-line supervisors of office and administrative support workers: workflow observation and change adoption.
Receptionists and information clerks: equipment collection and custody coordination.
skills_to_grow: Define reusable records, decision rules and exception paths.
Validate source-linked summaries and extracted specifications.
Design representative technical and usability tests.
Teach through practice and accessible instructions.
Apply GDPR data minimisation and recognise consultation requirements under national rules.
role.ambitious_version: A support improvement specialist who turns recurring faults into tested upgrade proposals, accessible training and a ready-equipment replacement service, while keeping consequential technical and spending decisions accountable.
